Express error conventions now split and pinned: res.sendStatus -> text/plain + status text (sendStatus(500)/404 paths), res.status().send(text) -> text/html no newline; ETag included; session delete validates UUID first (400 malformed) then 404 misses (MeController.js:85-97).

This is sampled capability evidence, not the reconciled in-scope inventory; the reconciled subset target and remaining queue are recorded in docs/agent-work/audits/coverage-risk-groups.md.

Cover variants: default-mode differential checks one local 307 redirect success, one explicitly whitelisted local image URL, one literal RFC1918 rejection, unsupported GIF extension rejection, and multipart URL-over-file precedence, and a 1.1 MB JSON PATCH parser probe. Successful PATCH copy/repeat validates response headers per side, removes seeded stale cache, and retains unrelated cover.svg. Separate EXP_PROXY_SUPPORT=1 evidence checks 307 rejection; private-address probing is skipped in that mode because upstream disables SSRF filtering. 301/302 chains, DNS rebinding, and the full SSRF address matrix remain unverified.

Fresh file-download characterization reproduced three upstream divergences before the fix: missing file IDs returned 404 text/html instead of 404 sendStatus text/plain; denied valid-file responses returned 403 text/html instead of sendStatus text/plain; and a denied user with a missing file ID got 403 in Go while upstream middleware returns 404 before the controller permission gate. Go now resolves item/library access/file ID first and uses Express sendStatus for these branches. Fresh fixed run passed all six file-download cases: valid, byte range, missing item, missing file, denied valid file, and denied missing file. Apple-mobile MIME override, X-Accel behavior, and alternate library-file types remain open.

Fresh per-file download characterization: six initial cases reproduced three Go divergences, all corrected. A seventh fixture-only missing-disk-file case first returned the expected upstream 404 body but the earlier harness ordering let upstream’s filesystem watcher collide with a later scan call; the probe now runs last and restores the renamed fixture file in a finally block. One clean rerun had a legacy Socket.IO timeout; a second fresh fixture passed 110/110 including all seven file-download cases. The download error helper now preserves a previously selected audio MIME type and adds Express string-response charset, Content-Length, and weak ETag. Unverified download branches include Apple-mobile MIME override, X-Accel-Redirect, other library-file types, and non-ENOENT filesystem errors.

Fresh 118-case Node v22.23.4 versus Go run adds admin email/notification settings checks. Source-created fresh DBs omit both settings rows; admin GET now matches constructor defaults, first changed PATCH persists via upsert, email uses upstream coercion for numeric and truthy values, and notification PATCH applies omitted-field defaults with Express sendStatus(200). The pre-fix run failed all six initial settings requests with Go 500 due to missing rows; the final fresh-fixture run passes 118/118. Email delivery/device routes and notification record CRUD/delivery remain unverified.

Fresh 129-case run adds notification create/read/update/delete, empty-URL no-op, minimal create defaults/coercion, missing route, and PATCH body-ID lookup cases. All 129 pass. The malformed POST with eventName but omitted urls is tested separately because upstream calls payload.urls.length, logs FATAL, and invokes process.exit(1); Go returns 200 without adding a record. This is a source-backed unresolved failure-behavior divergence and remains outside the passing suite.
